Lucy Tran: quick question — we have org-level canary `embeds_v2_canary` set to 10% for audience `beta`, and the /search route defines a route-level canary at 5% for audience `search-team`. If a user is in both audiences, which scope wins? seeing mixed resolves in the logs :thinking:

Alex Gomez: in theory route-level should win because it's more specific (route > project > org). that's what the precedence doc says, but what do the logs show exactly?

Lucy Tran: logs show user 7821 sometimes hitting embeds_v1 and sometimes v2 in the same window. example: `resolve_flag(embeds_v2_canary, user=7821, route=/search)` returned false at 12:02 and true at 12:08. no config changes in that window.

Mike R.: are we mixing percent-style canaries vs audience membership? route-level 5% is random-per-user but org 10% is also random; if RNG seeds differ by scope, you can see split behavior. check if we seed by (user, scope) or global user seed.

Sophia Lee: good call — runtime currently seeds per-flag key + scope_id. that means a user can be in org 10% but not route 5% or vice versa. route wins only if both are evaluated as overrides, but we first evaluate route scope and short-circuit — need to confirm order.

Lucy Tran: ok, so two sub-questions: 1) do we short-circuit when a more specific scope exists (i.e., route has any rule)? 2) should percent rules be deterministic across scopes (prefer same seed) to avoid contradictory behavior?

Alex Gomez: (1) yes, we short-circuit on the first matching rule in the scope precedence chain — route -> project -> org -> default. but if route has no matching audience rule for that user, we fall back to project/org.

Mike R.: (2) making percent membership deterministic across scopes is risky: it changes historical rollout math. But we can change seeding to be user-only (so percent is consistent across scopes), or keep scope-specific seeding and document it. pros/cons in PR comments?

Lucy Tran: we need a recommendation for the rollout playbook. product wants canaries to be able to target route-specific audiences without being trumped by org-level rollouts. they expect route override to be authoritative.

Sophia Lee: recommend: route-level explicit audience match -> authoritative (i.e., if route has audience rule and user matches, use it). If no match at route, evaluate project then org. For percent rules, seed by user_id only to make percent deterministic across scopes unless an explicit reason to isolate by scope exists. add a feature flag to toggle old behavior.

Alex Gomez: +1. also add an observable: resolved_scope on flag evaluation (org|project|route) and resolved_rule_id so we can debug fast.

CanaryBot: deployment note — long-running rollout `canary/embeds-v2` currently has guardrail: failed_requests > 1% triggers rollback. last check: 12:05 OK.

Lucy Tran: thanks. I'll open a small RFC and a PR for: 1) clarify precedence (route authoritative when matched), 2) change seeding to user-only for percent buckets behind a toggle, 3) add traced fields (`resolved_scope`, `resolved_rule_id`).

Mike R.: recommend also adding an integration test: simulate user in both audiences and assert resolves follow precedence and buckets are stable across requests.

Sophia Lee: adding also docs snippet for operators: example resolution order and how to reason about percent canaries. can help support when users report split behavior.

Alex Gomez: ping me on the PR and I’ll review. fyi, couple of product folks asked that we keep previous behavior for 2 weeks behind the toggle to avoid surprises.

Lucy Tran: noted. I'll include rollout plan and toggle TTL. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

CanaryBot: automated follow-up scheduled in 48h to check guardrail metrics for `canary/embeds-v2`.
